## Introduction 

This is the subset of complementary feeding indicators which are not related in calculating minimum acceptable diet indicator. There are 5 indicators which fall into this category and we are going to explain how `{riycf}` package can use for calculation of each single indicators mentioned below. 

1. Introduction Of Solid, Semi-solid Or Soft Foods 6-8 months
2. Egg And/Or Flesh Food Consumption 6-23 Months
3. Sweet Beverage Consumption 6-23 Months 
4. Unhealthy Food Consumption 6-23 Months 
5. Zero Vegetable Or Fruit Consumption 6-23 Months 

## Dataset set-up 

Firstly, load the required libraries for data analysis work. We will use `{riycf}` package for the IYCF indicator generation work. 

```{r setup}
library(riycf)
```

For this guideline demonstration, we will use the sample dataset provided by the CARE Myanmar team on IYCF modules. A detailed description of the variable's name and variable labels are mentioned in the documentation. Use the following syntax to check for the dataset description. 

```{r iycf-data}
iycfData
```

This dataset contains 359 observations and 46 variables, and all variables were organized based on the WHO IYCF sample questionnaire. We tried to mention explicitly matching function inputs parameters and question numbers from the WHO IYCF sample question. If your dataset did not have the same variables as the WHO sample one, please apply the most relevant ones in the respective input parameter. 

## Complementary Feeding Indicators 

### Introduction of solid, semi-solid, or soft foods for 6-8 month old children

The introduction of a semi-solid food indicator accounts for the 6-8 months old children who receive the solid (or semi-solid food) during the previous day. Here, we don't use the self-reported variable "number of meal frequency" feeding in this calculation. Instead, we use the dietary recall variables from WHO IYCF sample question *Question 7A* to *Question 7R*. If the children received one of the food items from those questions, those children are considered to have been introduced to solid, semi-solid, or soft food (ISSF). Use the `get_dummy()` function to create the dummy variable for solid food consumption from all solid food diet recall questions. 

```{r}
df <- iycfData

solid <- list(
  df$child_rice, df$child_potatoes, df$child_pumpkin, df$child_beans, 
  df$child_leafyveg, df$child_mango, df$child_fruit, df$child_organ, 
  df$child_beef, df$child_fish, df$child_processmeat, df$child_eggs, 
  df$child_yogurt, df$child_sweets
)

df$solid_food <- get_dummy(var_list = solid)
```

Then, use the `get_isssf()` function to get the number of children who meet this indicator definition or not. 

```{r}
df$isssf <- get_isssf(solid_food = df$solid_food, 
                      age = df$calc_age_months)
table(df$isssf)
```

### Egg and/or flesh food consumption for 6-23 month old children

Another indicator related to complementary feeding is the consumption of egg and/or flesh food, which accounts for 6-23 months children get eggs and/or flesh food in the previous day.  We can use `get_dummy()` to create the dummy variable to indicate who got those food or not. 

According to the WHO guidelines, the following questions were considered in the sweet beverage foods category. 

+ `Question 7I`: Liver, kidney, heart  
+ `Question 7J`: Sausages, hot dogs, ham, bacon, salami, canned meat
+ `Question 7K`: Any other meat, such as beef, pork, lamb, goat, chicken, duck
+ `Question 7L`: Eggs 
+ `Question 7M`: Fresh fish, dried fish or shellfish  

```{r}
egg_meat <- list(df$child_organ, df$child_beef, df$child_fish, df$child_processmeat, df$child_eggs)

df$egg_meat <- get_dummy(var_list = egg_meat)
```

Then, using `get_eff` to calculate EFF indicator using the dummy variable created before and the child age variable. 

```{r}
df$eff <- get_eff(egg_meat = df$egg_meat, 
                  age = df$calc_age_months)
table(df$eff)
```


### Sweet beverage consumption for 6-23 month old children 

We can use the Sweet Beverage Consumption indicator to identify the children who get the sweet beverage food from the previous day. Like other indicators from this complementary feeding indicator, use `get_dummy()` to identify the children who get those types of food, and then calculate the specific indicator "SwB" using `get_swb()`. 

According to the WHO guideline, the following questions were considered in the sweet beverage foods category.

+ `Question 6Cswt`: Milk from animals - sweet or flavoured type milk (asked only if `Question 6C` = yes)
+ `Question 6Dswt`: Yogurt drinks - sweet or flavoured type yogurt (asked only if `Question 6D` = yes)
+ `Question 6E`: Chocolate-flavoured drinks
+ `Question 6F`: Fruit juice or fruit-flavoured drinks
+ `Question 6G`: Sodas, malt drinks, sports drinks or energy drinks
+ `Question 6Hswt`: Tea, coffee, or herbal drinks - sweetened (asked only if `Question 6H` = yes)
+ `Question 6Jswt`: Other liquids - sweetened (asked only if `Question 6J` = yes)

#### Handling the skip pattern in the follow-up questions

Four of these questions (6Cswt, 6Dswt, 6Hswt and 6Jswt) are follow-up questions. For example, *"Was the milk sweetened or flavoured?"* is only asked if the child had milk from animals. When the main question is answered "no", the follow-up question is skipped and is stored as `NA` in the dataset. Here, `NA` means *"did not have it"*, not *"unknown"*.

`get_dummy()` returns `NA` for a child when any of the listed questions is `NA`. If the follow-up questions are passed to `get_dummy()` as they are, almost every child gets `NA`. In this sample dataset, no child had a yogurt drink, so `child_mproduct_sweet` is `NA` for every child and the sweet beverage indicator would be `NA` for all children.

The `get_followup()` function resolves each follow-up question using its main question before it is passed to `get_dummy()`:

| Main question | Follow-up question | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 0 (no) | `NA` (correctly skipped) or 0 | 0 |
| 1 (yes) | 1 | 1 |
| 1 (yes) | 0 | 0 |
| 1 (yes) | `NA` (should have been asked) | `NA`, with a warning |
| 0 (no) | 1 (skip pattern broken) | `NA`, with a warning |
| `NA` | any | `NA` |

```{r}
get_followup(main = c(1, 1, 0, 0, NA), followup = c(1, 0, NA, 0, NA))
```

The warnings help to check whether the skip pattern was followed during data collection. They are hidden in this document but appear in the R console.

Now, build the list of sweet beverage questions, using `get_followup()` for the four follow-up questions, and calculate the indicator.

```{r}
sweet <- list(
  get_followup(df$child_milk, df$child_milk_sweet),
  get_followup(df$child_mproduct, df$child_mproduct_sweet),
  df$child_chocolate, df$child_juice, df$child_soda,
  get_followup(df$child_tea, df$child_tea_sweet),
  get_followup(df$child_oth_drink, df$child_oth_drink_sweet)
)

df$sweet <- get_dummy(var_list = sweet)

df$swb <- get_swb(sweet = df$sweet,
                  age = df$calc_age_months)
table(df$swb, useNA = "ifany")
```

Children who are not 6-23 months old, or whose age is missing, get `NA` because they are outside the age range of this indicator.

**Limitation:** `get_followup()` only handles the skip pattern in which the main question coded 1 (yes) means the follow-up is asked and 0 (no) means it is skipped. It does not handle other kinds of skip pattern, such as a categorical main question (for example, the number of hours after birth asked only when the early initiation answer is "hours", which `get_eibf()` handles itself), follow-ups that depend on more than one question or on the child's age, or follow-ups asked when the main answer is "no". Such questions need to be recoded before they are used.

### Unhealthy food consumption for 6-23 month old children 

According to the definition, this indicator account for the two types of foods from the diet recall; *Question 7P* (sentinel sweet foods) and *Question 7Q* (sentinel fried and salty foods). We are using the `get_dummy()` function to create the dummy variable, which indicates whether the child took food from the previous day or not. Then, We can use the `get_ufc()` function to calculate the indicator.  

```{r}
unhealthy <- list(df$child_sweets, df$child_snack)

df$unhealthy <- get_dummy(var_list = unhealthy)

df$ufc <- get_ufc(unhealthy = df$unhealthy, 
                  age = df$calc_age_months)
table(df$ufc)
```


## Zero vegetable or fruit consumption for 6-23 month old children 

This indicator calculates for the 6-23 months of children who did not consume any vegetables or fruits during the previous day. Using the list of vegetables and fruits questions from the diet recall module (questions), we can use the `get_dummy()` function to calculate the dummy variable. Then, apply that variable to the `get_zvf()` to get the number of children who did or did not consume vegetables or fruits the previous day. 

According to the guideline, the fruit and vegetable questions list was recommended as follows. However, if your survey did not have that complete list of questions (variables), apply relevant to the indicator definition. 

+ `Questions 7C`: Vitamin A-rich yellow/orange vegetables 
+ `Questions 7E`: Dark green leafy vegetables 
+ `Questions 7F`: Other vegetables 
+ `Questions 7G`: Vitamin A-rich fruits  
+ `Questions 7H`: Other fruits 

```{r}
vege_fruit <- list(df$child_pumpkin, df$child_leafyveg, df$child_mango, df$child_fruit)

df$vege_fruit <- get_dummy(var_list = vege_fruit)

df$zvf <- get_zvf(vege_fruit = df$vege_fruit, 
                  age = df$calc_age_months)
table(df$zvf)
```
